language.script: Cyrillic (with extra Kazakh letters); Latin is being introduced
language.script_notes: Cyrillic is used with extra letters found in Kazakh — ә, ғ, қ, ң, ө, ұ, ү, һ and і — which do not appear in Russian; Russian is ubiquitous alongside Kazakh, so signs are often bilingual. A shift toward a Latin-based alphabet is under way, so some signs mix in Latin. Country calling code +7 is shared with Russia.

road_furniture.line_paint: Line colours vary a great deal: major roads often have yellow shoulder lines, while most roads use an all-white scheme.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Nearly all road signs are mounted on a white pole with a short black section painted at the base.

architecture.roof_style: Flat roofs on Soviet apartment blocks; pitched metal roofs on village houses; domes and minarets on mosques.
architecture.roof_material: Corrugated metal on houses; flat concrete on blocks.
architecture.wall_construction: Soviet-era prefabricated panel apartment blocks in nearly every town; single-storey brick or plastered houses behind fences in villages; futuristic glass-and-steel towers in the capital.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Grey concrete with pastel repainting, and glass and gold in the modern capital.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Soviet apartment blocks and statues alongside national monuments; mosques; yurt-shaped monuments and buildings; the capital's landmark towers and pyramids.

nature.vegetation: Vast dry steppe grassland across the north and center, semi-desert and desert in the south and west, and alpine forest and meadow in the southeastern mountains.
nature.terrain: Very flat over most of the country — the world's largest dry steppe and landlocked country — with the Kazakh Uplands in the center, high Tien Shan and Altai mountains in the southeast and east, and desert plateaus around the Caspian Sea in the west.
nature.climate_signature: Extreme continental climate — bitterly cold winters and hot dry summers, with huge open horizons and very sparse population.

vehicles.plate_color: White plate with black text and the light-blue national flag with 'KZ' on the left.
vehicles.plate_format: Three digits, three letters, then a two-digit region code in a square on the right (e.g. '123 ABC 05'); the last two digits give the region.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: A mix of Soviet-era Ladas and used Japanese and Korean imports; trucks and minibuses on long steppe highways.

google_coverage.camera_generation: New official coverage appeared around March 2024; Yandex imagery also covers Astana, Almaty and Karaganda.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Recent and still expanding; the country is enormous and sparsely populated, so coverage is thin outside the main cities and highways.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Cyrillic script, Soviet apartment blocks, endless steppe and forest-steppe in the north, and the shared +7 calling code
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The extra letters ә, ғ, қ, ң, ө, ұ, ү and һ appear only in Kazakh, and plates carry a light-blue flag and 'KZ' with a two-digit region code on the right.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Central Asian landscape, Soviet legacy and mountain and desert scenery in the south
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Plates carry the light-blue flag and 'KZ', and the extra Kazakh Cyrillic letters and white sign poles with a black base help separate it; compare plate and script details directly.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Similar open steppe and sparse population
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Kazakh Cyrillic with the extra letters and Russian on signs appear here, and plates use the KZ and light-blue flag format.
